newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia mayor says to propose tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia mayor says to propose tax cuts.

text.p: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell said he would propose a third year of tax cuts in a budget plan for the fiscal year beginning July 1.
Rendell, speaking a news conference, said he wanted to lower taxes to attract more business to the city and strabilize the tax base.
"It's the third straight year of tax cuts," he said.

However, he said, the budget would also have to deal with federal welfare cuts that will place greater demands on city social services, such as health centers that will have compensate for cuts to federal and state health aid programs.

Rendell's tax cuts would be in keeping with a five-year city budget plan that is required under state law and was updated in the 1996-1997 budget. The plan alls for small cuts in business and wage taxes for the 1997-1998 fiscal year.
Rendell is to propose the budget in a speech to the City Council at 1100 Thursday.
